the design and analysis of algorithms for efficiently following object pointers in a way that is independent of the amount of main memory.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a technique for processing object-oriented queries that are efficient when the referencing class is small, the referenced class is large, and there is a small main memory.

we have developed an algorithm for following pointers in large object-oriented database systems that is efficient when the number of blocks in the referenced class is small, the main memory is small, and the input class extensions have a large number of blocks.
we present an algorithm that performs well when the number of blocks in the referenced class is roughly the square of the size of main memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it may be possible to efficiently answer queries that follow object references when the referenced class is large, even if the main memory of the database system is small.

the performance of algorithms that follow object references can be significantly improved by exploiting the fact that the number of disk accesses to the referenced class is typically much smaller than the number of disk block accesses to the input class extension.
the cost of following object references can be significantly reduced when the number of disk pages in the referenced class is of the order of a square of the number in main memory.
